notes: Where to ask for the records a block's or a crossing's review cannot answer from public data, from docs/research/acquiring-missing-records-2026-11-27.md. A holder is an office or a role, never a person. Every route URL answered with a page on the date checked. FOIPPA is not stored in PGMaps: its sections are named, not quoted.

channels.label: BC Timber Sales business area
channels.holder: The BC Timber Sales business area that holds the plan, its planning staff
channels.ask: the plan, its amendment in force on the date asked, the site plan and the records behind it
channels.daysNote: No time is set. Not tried on the traced cases (an email).

cites.quote: A timber sales manager who holds a plan must publish the plan on a ministry website.
a site plan referred to in section 10.

channels.note: BC Timber Sales posts each business area's current plan; no amendment from 2017 to 2021 and no site plan was posted for the traced cases, although FRPA s. 20.25(3) requires a timber sales manager's plans, site plans among them, on a ministry website.

channels.label: The agreement holder
channels.holder: The holder of the licence and the forest stewardship plan, by its planning office
channels.ask: the plan and its amendment in force on the date asked, the site plan and the records behind it
channels.daysNote: No time is set: the regulations name no manner or time for an FSP holder's publication. Holders' posted plans were current texts only, or none.

cites.quote: who holds a plan must make the plan publicly available in accordance with the regulations.
a site plan referred to in section 10.

channels.note: Ask by the plan's id and the licence, never by a person's name. The planner keeps no holder's name: a letter is addressed to the holder's planning office by role.

channels.label: Natural resource district, stewardship
channels.holder: The natural resource district's stewardship staff

route.label: Ministry of Forests region and district contacts

channels.ask: the plan's amendment and approval letter in force on the date asked, and any site plan or fish-stream determination the district holds
channels.daysNote: No time is set. Not tried on the traced cases.

cites.quote: identify how the intended results or strategies described in the forest stewardship plan apply to the site.

channels.note: The FSP Tracking System holds every plan and amendment by its id, but only with a government or Business BCeID sign-in; district staff can read it.

channels.label: Natural resource district, engineering (road permit file)
channels.holder: The natural resource district's engineering staff, who keep the road permit and forest service road files

route.label: Forest roads permits, authorizations and access agreements

channels.ask: the crossing's design, as-built record, installation date, inspections and who maintains it, from the road permit or forest service road file
channels.daysNote: No time is set. Road permits and maintenance agreements go to the district office's inbox.

cites.quote: issue a road permit authorizing the holder to do one or both of the following

channels.note: The road layers' responsibility and maintainer fields only point to the file: the file says who built the crossing, when, to what design, and whether it was replaced.

channels.label: FrontCounter BC, water authorizations
channels.holder: FrontCounter BC or the region's water authorizations office

route.label: Notification of authorized changes in and about a stream

channels.ask: the notification or change approval file for the crossing: the notice as given, the habitat officer's statement of terms, and any engineer's requirement
channels.daysNote: No time is set for a request for a file's documents. Quote the approval file and FrontCounter tracking numbers.

cites.quote: obtain from a habitat officer a statement of the terms and conditions described in section 44 (2)

channels.note: A forestry crossing under WSR s. 39(2) needs no notice (s. 38(1) excludes s. 39(2)); a notice or approval file exists only for a change made on another route.

channels.label: Freedom of information request, Ministry of Forests
channels.holder: The Ministry of Forests (BC Timber Sales included), through the province's freedom of information operations
channels.ask: every record named, as at the dates given
channels.fee: $10 application fee for a general request (non-refundable); processing fees may apply
channels.daysNote: Up to 30 business days, which may be extended. Released files are searchable on Open Information.

cites.quote: the minister may determine whether the person has contravened the provision.

channels.note: The only route found to an amendment's text and approval letter as at a date, and to a contravention determination. FOIPPA s. 7 sets the 30 days and s. 10 their extension; it is not stored in PGMaps.

channels.label: Forest Practices Board
channels.holder: The Forest Practices Board, its own public body
channels.ask: any audit, complaint investigation or record of the Board on the block, its roads or the crossing
channels.fee: $10 application fee for a general freedom of information request
channels.daysNote: A freedom of information request to the Board runs as one to the ministry. A complaint about a current concern is its own route.

cites.quote: the board must deal with complaints from the public respecting prescribed matters that relate to this Act.

channels.note: The Board's audits name licensees, so they are read, never kept in the repository.

channels.label: Compliance and appeal records (search first)
channels.holder: Public databases: the Natural Resource Compliance and Enforcement Database and the Forest Appeals Commission's decisions

route.label: Natural Resource Compliance and Enforcement Database

channels.ask: inspections, orders and decisions recorded for the crossing, its road or the block
channels.daysNote: A search, not a request. NRCED holds Natural Resource Officer inspections from January 2021; no FRPA s. 71 determination was found in it.
channels.note: What is not found here is not proof that nothing was determined: a contravention determination is reached by FOI. The Forest Appeals Commission publishes its decisions at https://www.bcfac.ca/.

channels.label: Field survey
channels.ask: what the ground shows at each place: streams the maps miss, channel width and gradient, fish presence by the standard protocol, the structure and its size
channels.daysNote: Set by the crew. A LiDAR flow screen, where a 1 m DEM is published, shows where to look first; it is never the answer.
channels.note: Field confirmation is the source for small streams below the Freshwater Atlas and for fish-stream limbs. Submitting a PSCIS assessment needs a BCeID and a role granted by the fish passage program.

channels.label: Air photo order, GeoBC
channels.holder: GeoBC, through the Base Map Online Store
channels.ask: full-resolution scans of the frames that bracket when the road and crossing were first seen
channels.fee: About $18.50 a full-resolution scan, as priced when the research was done; free thumbnails first
channels.daysNote: 10 to 15 business days for scans. Thumbnails of each frame are free and immediate.
channels.note: Imagery dates the road, not the pipe: whether the structure was replaced stays a question for the road permit file.

gaps.label: Forest stewardship plan and amendment in force
gaps.subject: block
gaps.ask: the forest stewardship plan and amendment in force when the cutting permit was issued, with its approval letter, and its results and strategies for the block's forest development unit
gaps.why: Which plan and amendment applied, and what it said, decide the FSP questions; the FDU layer misses amendments and the FSP Tracking System is login-only.

gaps.label: Site plan
gaps.subject: block
gaps.ask: the site plan for the cutblock and its roads (FRPA s. 10), with its standards units, reserves and their purposes
gaps.why: The site plan says how the plan's results and strategies apply to the block; none was posted for the traced cases.

gaps.label: Riparian classes and management areas
gaps.subject: block
gaps.ask: the riparian class of each stream, wetland and lake in or beside the block, and its reserve and management zone widths, from the site plan and its field assessment
gaps.why: No public layer holds a riparian class; it is set in the site plan from field evidence.

gaps.label: Streams the maps miss
gaps.subject: block
gaps.ask: every stream the block's roads and harvesting cross or border, including those below the Freshwater Atlas, located on the ground
gaps.why: A third or more of assessed crossings in the three districts sit away from any modelled stream; only the ground shows them.

gaps.label: Fish-stream determination
gaps.subject: crossing
gaps.ask: the fish-stream determination for the stream at the crossing, with the fish inventory or gradient survey behind it
gaps.why: Whether a stream is a fish stream is asked limb by limb; a single visit seeing no fish is not absence.

gaps.label: Crossing design and as-built
gaps.subject: crossing
gaps.ask: the crossing's design (size, cover, fill, capacity, fish passage, any engineer's design) and its as-built record and inspections
gaps.why: The structure's figures and design decide the culvert and bridge questions; PSCIS describes a structure, it does not give its design.

gaps.label: When the crossing was built or replaced
gaps.subject: crossing
gaps.ask: when the crossing was built, and whether and when its structure was replaced
gaps.why: FPPR s. 56(2) turns on a crossing built after June 15, 1995; a road permit's award date is the permit's, not the crossing's, and imagery dates the road, not the pipe.

gaps.label: Who holds and maintains the crossing
gaps.subject: crossing
gaps.ask: who holds the road the crossing is on and who maintains the crossing, under which permit or agreement
gaps.why: The authority and the duties at a crossing follow the person who builds and maintains it.

gaps.label: Water Act notice, terms or approval
gaps.subject: crossing
gaps.ask: the notification or change approval for the crossing, the habitat officer's statement of terms, and any engineer's requirement
gaps.why: Only the file says whether a notice was given, what terms bound the work, or what an approval allows.

gaps.label: Contravention determinations
gaps.subject: crossing
gaps.ask: any inspection, determination of contravention, penalty or order about the crossing or its road
gaps.why: A determination bears on whether the crossing complies and affects fish passage; NRCED does not hold FRPA s. 71 determinations.

fom.note: Each forest operations map project names its plan's id (fspId), without a sign-in, but maps start in 2022, and its API sends no CORS headers, so the planner cannot read it from the browser: open the map and find the block's project.

fsp.standardsNote: Search the plan's stocking standards (the standards appendix or tables) for this regime id: the plan that lists it is the plan the opening's standards were taken from. The id can name the version that added the standard; it never names the amendment in force on a date.
